claim_being_audited: The model can be certified for launch because aggregate readiness passed, rollout controls exist, and the remaining mortgage servicing assistant weakness can be handled through monitoring plus explicit launch-time model-card disclosure.
decision_criteria: Use 'compliant' only if admissible evidence shows the policy threshold is satisfied.
Policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Policy text expressly says rollout controls, rollback, dashboards, and small rollout percentages do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.

Because the exposed segment remains in scope and no approved risk acceptance exists, current compliance turns on evidence of actual launch-time disclosure, not merely the idea that disclosure would be prudent.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual launch-time model card or disclosure artifact covering the mortgage servicing assistant limitation.
Provide evidence that the disclosure is approved and required as a launch gate condition before certification.
Provide any approved risk acceptance that specifically addresses continued exposure of the mortgage servicing assistant segment, if relying on that exception instead of disclosure.
specific_concerns: The evidence shows the affected mortgage servicing assistant segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
Policy text says rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The risk-acceptance draft is not approved and does not address the exposed segment, so it cannot satisfy the policy exception.
No admissible evidence shows that explicit launch-time model-card disclosure has been completed, approved, or made a binding launch condition.
The actor's recommended action is 'certify_model' even though the evidentiary basis only supports certification if disclosure is actually included at launch.
unsupported_claims: The packet does not prove that certification is currently compliant; it proves at most that certification could be defensible if explicit launch-time disclosure is in place.
The recommended action 'certify_model' is unsupported as stated because the required disclosure predicate is not evidenced.
There is no admissible evidence that model-card disclosure has been reviewed, finalized, or linked to the launch gate for this release.
